reasoning_traces.think: This chapter explores the mathematical foundations of optimal reinsurance strategies under convex premium principles and exponential claim size distributions. It begins with establishing the convexity of the reinsurance premium function, leveraging the structure of the cumulative distribution function F(z, y) = (1 - e^{-ζ(y)z})1{z>0}. This ensures that the value function Ψα(t, y) is strictly convex in α, enabling the application of standard optimization techniques. The Expected Value Principle (EVP) is then applied to derive the closed-form optimal reinsurance strategy α∗(t) = e^{-r(T-t)} log(1 + θ)/η. This result hinges on the assumption that claim sizes are exponentially distributed, which simplifies the integral expressions involved in deriving the premium. The derivation proceeds by evaluating the second-order derivative of the relevant integral term, confirming strict convexity. Subsequently, the stationary point condition is derived from the first-order optimality condition, leading to a unique solution for α∗(t). These primitives form the basis for understanding how stochastic control and dynamic programming interact with risk measures in insurance contexts.
